title: Coding-harness landscape
scope: A source-separated guide to public harness usage signals, catalogues and controlled benchmark methods. It does not combine unlike measures or select one best harness.

method.order: Sources are grouped by the question they can answer. No composite rank is calculated.
method.limits: Usage, popularity, documented capability and controlled task performance describe different populations and denominators. A missing measure remains unassessed and no source is treated as proof of general quality.

sources.name: OpenLabor Harness Ranking
sources.observed_signal: Attributed OpenRouter tokens, requests and model share over selectable time windows.
sources.boundary: This observes one routing channel. It does not establish active users, total adoption, privacy, safety or harness quality.

sources.name: HarnessMatch
sources.observed_signal: Documented capabilities, operating models, evidence coverage and eight separate public usage views.
sources.boundary: Its usage channels retain their native denominators. Popularity, capability and benchmark evidence are not added into one score.

sources.name: Best of Agent Harnesses
sources.observed_signal: A curated project catalogue with categories, editorial attributes, activity signals and machine-readable data.
sources.boundary: Its ordering uses editorial relevance and GitHub signals. It is useful for discovery, not a controlled adoption or performance benchmark.

sources.name: HarnessRank
sources.observed_signal: A same-benchmark, same-model and same-effort repeated-run comparison method.
sources.boundary: No full benchmark rows were published at the checked date. The method is visible, but there is no result table to reproduce or rank.

method_references.name: Qihoo360 Harness-Bench
method_references.boundary: Reference for deterministic outcomes, process measures, robustness, security and efficiency. Reuse requires a fresh licence check.

method_references.name: Harbor
method_references.boundary: A benchmark orchestration substrate, not a ranking authority. Telemetry, network behaviour and isolation require separate verification.

project_status.title: PLAG IN prototype compatibility snapshot
project_status.summary: The earlier five-client compatibility order is retained only as a dated project note. It is not part of the independent harness landscape and does not rank harness quality.
project_status.boundary: No installed client completed a verified end-to-end integration in that snapshot. Later benchmark work requires its own evidence and approval.
